title: Book Two · Chapter 74: A Night with No Work
story:
On Friday evening, Mum finishes the last button on a customer's shirt. She checks the back of each stitch. Then she puts away the thread.

“No more tonight,” she says.

Ronan looks at the small pile beside her. “Those too?”

“Tomorrow. They are not due tonight.”

She moves the work basket under her chair. Dad brings tea. Ronan fetches his birthday book, but Mum holds up one finger.

“First, I want to sit.”

He leaves the book on the shelf. The window is open. A wheel knocks against the stones in the street. Ronan hears it through the window. The black cat crosses the yard. It stops under the window and looks inside.

Dad holds up his cup. “No tea for you.”

The cat looks away. Mum shifts her feet and leans back in her chair. She seems pleased with this quiet evening.

“Very rude,” Ronan says.

“Perhaps it wants a better cup,” Mum says.

After a while, Dad asks for paper. Ronan brings a clean scrap. Dad draws a long line with two little circles at one end.

“What is it?”

“A broken bicycle,” Ronan says.

“A pair of scissors,” Mum says.

Dad draws a small hook on the other end.

“A long spoon,” Ronan says.

“An umbrella,” Dad tells them.

Mum looks at the flat line. “It will keep one finger dry.”

Ronan laughs and takes his turn. He draws two circles, a seat and a large bell. Mum knows at once. “The blue bike.” Dad says it is an umbrella with wheels.

Mum takes the pencil last. She draws a square, then another inside it. Dad guesses a window. Ronan guesses a box. Mum adds a small round mark near one side.

“The green door!” Ronan says.

Mum nods. Then she draws three little figures beside it. One figure has very long legs. Ronan knows that one is Dad.

“Why am I so small?” Ronan asks.

“Paper is expensive,” Dad says.

Mum gives Ronan the pencil. He makes his own figure a little taller. Then he adds the cat with its tail straight up.

He looks at Mum's empty hands on the paper.

“What shall I put here?”

“Nothing heavy.”

“Your cup?”

“Yes. I can hold that.”

Ronan draws a very small circle. He puts a handle beside it.

Dad leans forward.

“That cup is larger than her head.”

“Mum likes her tea.”

She lifts her real cup toward the picture. Ronan laughs and makes the little circle smaller.

The pencil is very short now. He gives it back to Mum. She adds a low chair behind her figure and sits back in her own chair again.

Dad studies the paper for another moment.

“I want that one.”

“Which one?”

“The chair. Yours looks comfortable.”

Mum keeps her pencil above the page, then draws a second chair beside the first. Dad's little figure has somewhere to sit too.

They put the paper on the shelf for the evening. It belongs to all three of them. Nobody needs to finish it for a customer.

At bedtime, Ronan goes back to look. Dad has added a tiny umbrella above the cat. It has one long straight line and two circles, just like before. Ronan calls Mum. She comes over and looks at it. Then she starts to laugh again.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

tea＝茶；scrap＝小片；umbrella＝雨伞。

## 理解问题

1. Mum这晚怎样安排自己的时间？
2. 一家人的游戏为什么好笑？

## 读句子

**Ronan / brings / a clean scrap.** Ronan／拿来／一张干净的小纸片。
